candidates.name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
support_spans: Classic-appearing hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells originated from one lateral end, pushing down into the dermis and involving many hairs
Malignant squamous cells contained eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli; mitotic figures were present
candidates.why: The histopathological examination reveals a hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts and proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells, which are characteristic features of squamous cell carcinoma.

candidates.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
support_spans: Classic-appearing hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells originated from one lateral end, pushing down into the dermis and involving many hairs
Malignant squamous cells contained eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli; mitotic figures were present
candidates.why: The presence of malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, along with mitotic figures, supports the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma.

candidates.name: Sebaceous carcinoma
support_spans: Central areas of clear cell change were periodic acid–Schiff positive and diastase sensitive
contradict_spans: Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor
candidates.why: The presence of clear cell change with positive periodic acid-Schiff and diastase sensitive staining could suggest sebaceous carcinoma, but negative adipophilin and androgen receptor stains contradict this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma
support_spans: Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells originated from one lateral end, pushing down into the dermis and involving many hairs
candidates.why: The invasion of neoplastic squamous cells into the dermis and involvement of hair follicles supports the diagnosis of invasive squamous cell carcinoma.

candidates.name: Basal cell carcinoma
support_spans: Ki67 highlighted scattered basal cells and stained about 20% to 40% of tumor cell nuclei
contradict_spans: Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells originated from one lateral end, pushing down into the dermis and involving many hairs
candidates.why: The Ki67 staining pattern could suggest basal cell carcinoma, but the proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells and involvement of hairs contradict this diagnosis.

unexplained_specific_evidence: Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor

selector.rationale: The presence of a classic-appearing hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts, proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells, and malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Sebaceous carcinoma
rejected.why: Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor contradict this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells, not basal cells, is noted in the histopathological examination.
